disposition.reason: The operational MLX path already owns grouped selected-expert qmm; remaining cost is launch/synchronization/attention and route-major consumption. P0 contention also makes isolated peaks non-qualification evidence.
disposition.next_frontier: native multi-stage per-token graph with persistent route/activation/weight residency, scalar-argument buffers for ICB compatibility, exact Kimi routing semantics, and a capability-valid parity gate

transferable_lessons: Keep BatchKVCache outside compiled graph boundaries.
Preserve the existing MLX grouped gather_qmm contract; local Python fusion does not supply 250 TPS.
Do not trade shared-expert precision for a headline peak without capability evidence.
A new resident P1 is not a clean-room bandwidth measurement while P0 remains active.

Native trace makes the remaining bottleneck concrete: the complete graph still launches 461 dispatches per decode token and the F16 LM head is the largest single consumer; route tiling does not remove that cost.

The existing ICB substrate reduced a synthetic 15-dispatch host-encode p50 from 9.58us direct to 3.63us fused (2.64x); Kimi kernels still use dynamic set_bytes/set_u32 arguments, so scalar argument buffers are required before a native decode graph can replay safely.

A scalar-buffer Q4 route-consumer ICB matched direct output exactly but was slower for one dispatch (4.79us versus 3.42us p50); grouped across 15 dependent route stages it reduced host encode p50 from 9.42us to 4.75us (1.98x), validating the multi-stage graph direction.
Uniform KV4 reduced neither the measured wall nor the decode bottleneck; the next 250-TPS step remains a resident native graph, not more cache quantization toggles.

The scalar-buffer route graph scales: exact parity and 3.09x host-encode reduction at 27 stages, 4.63x at 54 stages, and 16.28x at the current 461-dispatch count. The 461-stage result is synthetic route repetition; the remaining proof is to bind all dynamic Kimi layer arguments and measure complete decode TPS.

Persistent scalar buffers alone do not move the body: one matched native pair was 20.8577 versus 20.8548 tok/s under the same P0-co-resident stalls. The next real lever is a complete dependency-ordered graph with persistent route/activation/KV buffers and scalar-buffer variants for every dynamic kernel, not another isolated launch-contract patch.

A persistent scalar-buffer variant for the 461-dispatch Q4_0 route-accumulate hotspot also failed to show a repeatable decode gain (23.15/15.99 tok/s versus 19.66/19.67 controls); host-encode reduction alone is not enough while attention, copies, synchronization, and the rest of the graph remain outside replay.

A native Q6_K LM-head consumer is mechanically cheap and measurable (122us of head-kernel GPU time across 16 forwards), but the mixed lower-byte body still collapsed output and remained 33.86 tok/s; 250 requires a capability-valid complete graph/body change, not just head quantization.
